page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.xlarge is an x86_64 virtual instance within the High Clock Speed family, operating on the KVM hypervisor. Compute is provided by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at a base frequency of 3.1 GHz, provisioned as 4 dedicated vCPUs spanning 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. System memory totals 16.0 GB, allocating 4.0 GB per vCPU core. The instance includes 35 MB of L3 cache alongside support for AVX-512 vector extensions. Networking provides a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps, while no local instance storage or dedicated GPU accelerators are bundled with this configuration.

Benchmark evaluations highlight a divergence between single-threaded and multi-threaded throughput. Single-core performance sits in the middle 50% across tests, achieving 1432.58 in stress-ng and 1245.0 in Geekbench, supported by the 3.1 GHz clock rate. In contrast, multi-core benchmarks such as Geekbench multi-core (2760.0) and PassMark CPU (4655.05) rank in the bottom quartile, bounded by the two-physical-core physical limit. Memory bandwidth benchmarks also demonstrate lower-tier throughput, recording 26.35 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 22.75 GB/sec for large-block writes.

The primary architectural tradeoff lies in providing dedicated, elevated clock speeds while constrained by a low core count and lower memory bandwidth. Because no local disks are included, operational storage relies entirely on external network-attached block volumes. Given the balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.xlarge is suited for general application hosting, moderate web serving, CI/CD build workers, and small backend services where consistent clock frequency is prioritized over heavy parallel scalability.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.xlarge is a high-clock-speed instance delivering 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 3.1 GHz. Equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, it maintains a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio on the x86_64 architecture with KVM virtualization. The configuration contains no local storage and no GPU hardware, relying on 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth for external access. Benchmark data reveals average single-core efficiency across Geekbench and stress-ng, whereas multi-core compute, memory bandwidth, and parallel decompression metrics reflect lower-percentile results due to physical core constraints. With stable per-core execution speeds and modest network throughput, the instance provides cost-effective hosting for general business applications, intermediate web servers, build automation tasks, and lightweight microservices requiring predictable clock performance.
